questions.markdown:
A high-pass active filter with gain is implemented as shown in figure. The filter has the following measured characteristics:

- At $f = 50\text{ Hz}$: $|H| = 0.5\text{ V/V}$, $\angle H = +45^\circ$
- At $f = 10\text{ kHz}$: $|H| = 12\text{ V/V}$, $\angle H = +5^\circ$

(a) Analyze the circuit to determine the 3-dB cutoff frequency ($f_0$) and high-frequency gain ($H_0$).
(b) If $R_1 = 47\text{ k}\Omega$ and $C = 68\text{ nF}$, calculate $R_2$ and verify whether still the circuit works as HPF for the $H_0$ and $f_0$ obtained in the part (a). If not suggest the values changes in the $C$ and $R_2$ components.

diagrams.caption: High-pass active filter using an op-amp with input network $R_1$ and $C$ and feedback resistor $R_2$. (original source region)

questions.markdown: Using standard 5% resistor values, design a two stage circuit that produces the output voltage $V_0 = 8V_1 + 12V_2 - 4V_3$. Provide the complete circuit diagram and a detailed step-by-step solution justifying your component choices. The input impedance if 1st stage is 10 k$\Omega$. Hint: You can use unity gain inverting amplifier and the 1st stage with followed by difference amplifier in the 2nd stage.
What is an Opamp window detector? Explain the working of it with relevant circuit diagram and its voltage transfer characteristics.

Design a simple automatic light control system using a 555 timer for a staircase. When a person presses a push button, a light bulb should turn ON and remain ON for 2 minutes, after which it should automatically turn OFF. The system uses a 9V battery.

Explain the advantages of using a current-mirror-loaded differential amplifier over a traditional resistor loaded differential pair for single-ended output applications. Derive the differential voltage gain for the current-mirror-loaded configuration.
